rule: A link says which Portrait of a Graduate skills a partner outcome works toward. It never says what stage participants reach, and it is never a score for a partner.

source.title: School District of Philadelphia Portrait of a Graduate Competency Framework, Updated Skills Map 11.2
source.author: Written by Building 21 for the School District of Philadelphia
source.note: Identifiers follow version 11.2 only; other versions number the skills differently. Only competencies 1 to 8 have progressions.

fits.description: The code names the same result the Portrait skill describes.
Some statements under the code fit the Portrait skill and some do not, or the code sits next to the skill without matching it.
The Portrait has no skill for this result: a feeling, a status, a health condition, a relationship received, or a result for families, staff or systems.

portrait.name: Direct my own learning
portrait.statement: I can take ownership of my learning by connecting it to what matters to me and the world around me, knowing how I think and learn, and adjusting how I work as I go.

portrait.name: Connect what I'm learning to what matters to me
portrait.statement: I can connect what I'm learning to my interests, goals, and the world around me.

portrait.name: Understand how I learn and how I think
portrait.statement: I can recognize how I learn best and how I think, and use that to guide my learning.

portrait.name: Plan and manage my time, attention, and work
portrait.statement: I can plan my work, manage my time and attention, and follow through.

portrait.name: Monitor my progress and adjust my strategies
portrait.statement: I can monitor my progress as I work and adjust my strategies to stay on track.

portrait.name: Seek and use feedback to grow
portrait.statement: I can seek feedback from others and use it to improve.

portrait.name: Persist with purpose and adapt with confidence
portrait.statement: I can understand myself, care for my well-being, take healthy risks, and persist through challenge and change in pursuit of what matters most to me.

portrait.name: Know my values and aspirations
portrait.statement: I can name my values, aspirations, and what matters most to me.

portrait.name: Care for my well-being
portrait.statement: I can take care of my physical, mental, and emotional well-being.

portrait.name: Manage my emotions, stress, and impulses
portrait.statement: I can recognize and manage my emotions, stress, and impulses.

portrait.name: Navigate challenges and adapt through change
portrait.statement: I can persevere through difficulty and adapt as circumstances change.

portrait.name: Communicate Ideas
portrait.statement: I can shape and share ideas, emotions, and information clearly and effectively across audiences, contexts, and forms of expression.

portrait.name: Choose and introduce my message
portrait.statement: I can identify my purpose, audience, and message, and introduce it clearly.

portrait.name: Convey ideas in writing
portrait.statement: I can write clearly and effectively for my purpose and audience.

portrait.name: Present to an audience
portrait.statement: I can present with focus, clarity, and impact to an audience.

portrait.name: Communicate visually
portrait.statement: I can communicate visually with clarity and impact.

portrait.name: Craft stories
portrait.statement: I can craft stories with arc and detail to build connection or communicate ideas.

portrait.name: Engage in Dialogue and Advocacy
portrait.statement: I can listen actively, engage with empathy across cultures and perspectives, and advocate for myself and others with respect and impact.

portrait.name: Engage in discussion
portrait.statement: I can listen with full presence and contribute meaningfully to discussion.

portrait.name: Navigate difficult conversations with honesty and care
portrait.statement: I can stay engaged in difficult conversations with honesty and care.

portrait.name: Advocate for myself and articulate my own needs
portrait.statement: I can articulate my needs, goals, and boundaries and advocate for myself.

portrait.name: Advocate for others
portrait.statement: I can recognize when others are not being heard and advocate for them.

portrait.name: Collaborate effectively on teams
portrait.statement: I can contribute my strengths, build inclusive teams, navigate disagreement, check in on progress, and help my team produce work no one of us could do alone.

portrait.name: Establish shared purpose, norms, and roles
portrait.statement: I can help establish shared purpose, norms, and roles on a team.

portrait.name: Navigate conflicts and challenges productively
portrait.statement: I can navigate conflicts and challenges productively.

portrait.name: Monitor progress and share accountability
portrait.statement: I can track my team's progress and share accountability.

portrait.name: Reflect on our collaboration
portrait.statement: I can reflect on how my team worked together and how to improve.

portrait.name: Build relationships, networks, and strengthen community
portrait.statement: I can foster belonging, build and draw on networks, take action, and engage in the communities I am part of to make them stronger.

portrait.name: Foster belonging
portrait.statement: I can foster belonging and welcome others into a community.

portrait.name: Build and draw on my network
portrait.statement: I can build and draw on a network of people and resources.

portrait.name: Take action to improve my community
portrait.statement: I can take action to improve my community.

portrait.name: Build and engage in healthy online communities
portrait.statement: I can build and engage in healthy online communities.

portrait.name: Think Critically
portrait.statement: I can ask good questions, evaluate information and arguments, weigh perspectives, and improve my own reasoning to reach sound, well-supported conclusions.

portrait.name: Ask questions
portrait.statement: I can ask questions that guide my thinking and inquiry.

portrait.name: Find and evaluate information
portrait.statement: I can find relevant information and evaluate whether to trust it.

portrait.name: Analyze and evaluate media
portrait.statement: I can analyze and evaluate media, including a creator's purpose and how it tries to persuade me.

portrait.name: Interpret and synthesize information, data, and representations
portrait.statement: I can interpret and synthesize information, data, and representations to make meaning.

portrait.name: Evaluate evidence, reasoning, and arguments
portrait.statement: I can evaluate evidence, reasoning, and arguments to reach a warranted judgment.

portrait.name: Think flexibly
portrait.statement: I can consider multiple perspectives and revise my thinking when the evidence warrants.

portrait.name: Monitor and improve my reasoning
portrait.statement: I can monitor my reasoning and take steps to improve it.

portrait.name: Solve Everyday and Real-World Problems
portrait.statement: I can understand a problem, work toward the best solution while weighing its impact, test and improve it when I can, and reflect on my solution and what I learned.

portrait.name: Understand the problem
portrait.statement: I can understand what a problem really is before trying to solve it.

portrait.name: Choose an approach
portrait.statement: I can choose a problem-solving approach that fits the problem.

portrait.name: Develop, Test, and Improve Prototypes (When Appropriate)
portrait.statement: I can develop, test, and improve prototypes when the problem calls for it.

portrait.name: Implement, evaluate, and reflect
portrait.statement: I can implement my solution, evaluate how well it worked, and reflect on what I learned.

portrait.name: Create and Innovate
portrait.statement: I can generate original ideas, develop and refine them into finished work, identify opportunities to create value for others, and turn promising ideas into action.

portrait.name: Generate original ideas
portrait.statement: I can generate many and varied ideas, and combine, adapt, or build on ideas to create something new.

portrait.name: Develop and refine creative work
portrait.statement: I can develop an idea into finished creative work, using critique and revision to strengthen its originality and craft.

portrait.name: Identify opportunities and create value
portrait.statement: I can identify unmet needs or opportunities and develop ideas that create social, cultural, or economic value for others.

portrait.name: Turn ideas into action
portrait.statement: I can launch a venture, product, event, or initiative by organizing people and resources, weighing risks and rewards, and planning how to reach the people it serves.

portrait.name: Engage as an Informed and Responsible Global Citizen
portrait.statement: I can explain how people, communities, and systems are interconnected, investigate issues across perspectives, and use what I learn to participate in civic and global life.

portrait.name: Explain global interconnections
portrait.statement: I can explain how local choices and global social, economic, political, and environmental systems influence one another.

portrait.name: Participate in civic and democratic life
portrait.statement: I can explain how government works at the local, state, and national levels, including my rights and responsibilities, and use that knowledge to participate in civic and democratic processes.

portrait.name: Examine global issues and perspectives
portrait.statement: I can investigate global issues using evidence and perspectives from different places and people affected.

portrait.name: Analyze how the past shapes the present
portrait.statement: I can analyze primary and secondary sources in their historical context to explain causes, changes, and continuities, and how the past shapes present-day communities and issues.

portrait.name: Make Ethical and Responsible Choices
portrait.statement: I can weigh values, perspectives, and consequences when making choices that affect other people, communities, and the world, and act with integrity.

portrait.name: Reason through ethical dilemmas
portrait.statement: I can weigh competing values, responsibilities, and consequences to make and explain ethical choices.

portrait.name: Weigh the impact of my choices
portrait.statement: I can analyze how my choices affect people, communities, and the environment, now and in the future, and use that analysis to guide what I do.

portrait.name: Use technology and AI ethically and responsibly
portrait.statement: I can use digital technologies and AI responsibly by protecting privacy, crediting others' work, identifying bias and potential harm, and deciding when and how to use these tools.

portrait.name: Act with integrity
portrait.statement: I can act on my values when it is difficult, take responsibility for the impact of my actions, and take steps to make things right.

portrait.name: Apply Academic Knowledge and Skills
portrait.statement: I can read complex texts critically, analyze quantitative data, model with mathematics, develop and use models, investigate scientific questions, apply core disciplinary concepts in new situations, and strengthen my academic skills.

portrait.name: Read critically and make meaning of complex texts
portrait.statement: I can read and analyze literary, informational, and subject-specific texts to understand ideas, evaluate arguments, and support interpretations with textual evidence.

portrait.name: Analyze and interpret quantitative data
portrait.statement: I can organize, represent, analyze, and interpret quantitative data to identify patterns, evaluate claims, and draw supported conclusions.

portrait.name: Model with mathematics
portrait.statement: I can use algebraic and other mathematical concepts, procedures, and representations (such as expressions, equations, inequalities, functions, and geometric figures) to represent real-world situations, solve problems, and interpret my results in context.

portrait.name: Develop and use models
portrait.statement: I can develop, use, and refine models to represent real-world situations, explain relationships, make predictions, and evaluate how well the models represent reality.

portrait.name: Use scientific inquiry and reasoning
portrait.statement: I can investigate scientific questions, gather and analyze evidence, and use scientific reasoning and core science concepts to develop and evaluate explanations.

portrait.name: Strengthen academic skills and prepare for assessments
portrait.statement: I can identify areas for growth in my reading and math skills, use effective study and test-taking strategies and online learning programs, track my growth, and use assessment results to strengthen my academic performance and test scores.

portrait.name: Use digital and AI tools to learn and work
portrait.statement: I can choose and use digital and AI tools, including tools used in my field of interest, to learn, investigate ideas, and produce quality work, checking the accuracy and usefulness of their outputs.

portrait.name: Plan and Navigate My Postsecondary Future
portrait.statement: I can explore opportunities that align with my interests, strengths, and goals, make informed decisions about my future, and take steps toward my chosen pathway, including managing my money and navigating new settings.

portrait.name: Explore my interests, strengths, and possibilities
portrait.statement: I can connect my interests, strengths, and goals to possible education, training, career, and life pathways.

portrait.name: Investigate postsecondary and career pathways
portrait.statement: I can research the requirements, costs, earnings, and job outlook of different pathways after high school, including college, apprenticeship, military, employment, and self-employment.

portrait.name: Evaluate options and make informed choices
portrait.statement: I can compare possible pathways using my goals, values, opportunities, and constraints to make informed choices.

portrait.name: Plan and take steps toward my future
portrait.statement: I can develop and carry out a plan for my next steps after high school, including coursework, work-based learning, credentials, continued learning, deadlines, and needed resources.

portrait.name: Navigate new settings
portrait.statement: I can learn the expectations, rights, responsibilities, and supports in a new workplace, college, or training setting and use them to succeed and advocate for myself.

portrait.name: Manage my money
portrait.statement: I can build and follow a budget and make informed decisions about earning, saving, spending, borrowing, and paying for education or training.

portrait.name: Communicate my competencies, experiences, and goals
portrait.statement: I can communicate my competencies, experiences, skills, and goals effectively in applications, interviews, portfolios, and other postsecondary opportunities.

portrait.name: Curate my portfolio
portrait.statement: I can select, organize, and reflect on evidence of my competencies and experiences to show my growth and readiness.

portrait.name: Present and defend my portfolio
portrait.statement: I can present my portfolio to an audience, explain what my evidence shows about my growth and readiness, and respond to questions about it.

portrait.name: Craft my application materials
portrait.statement: I can create a resume, cover letter, personal statement, or online career profile tailored to a specific opportunity that shows why I am a strong fit.

portrait.name: Interview with confidence
portrait.statement: I can prepare for and participate in interviews, answering questions with specific examples of my experiences and competencies, and follow up afterward.

portrait.name: Identify and secure references
portrait.statement: I can identify people who know my work and character, ask them for references or recommendations, and keep them informed.

portrait.name: Communicate across workplace and community settings
portrait.statement: I can communicate by email, phone, video, and in person in ways that fit the relationship, purpose, and setting, including workplaces, colleges, and community organizations.

portrait.name: Manage my digital footprint and online presence
portrait.statement: I can build and manage an online presence that represents me the way I intend to employers, colleges, and communities.

codes.name: Academic Learning & Achievement
codes.reason: A broad academic result with no subject sits under Apply Academic Knowledge and Skills at the competency level only.

codes.name: Literacy: Reading & Writing
codes.reason: Reading gains are Read Critically and Make Meaning of Complex Texts; writing gains are Convey Ideas in Writing.

codes.name: English Language Development & Multilingualism
codes.reason: The Portrait has no skill for learning English or keeping a home language.

codes.name: Mathematics
codes.reason: Math skill and proficiency are Model with Mathematics and Analyze and Interpret Quantitative Data.

codes.name: Science, Technology & Engineering
codes.reason: Science inquiry and engineering design fit Use Scientific Inquiry, Develop and Use Models and the prototype skill; science content knowledge and coding have no Portrait skill.

codes.name: Other Academic Subjects
codes.reason: History fits Analyze How the Past Shapes the Present and geography or economics fit Explain Global Interconnections; world languages have no Portrait skill.

codes.name: Arts Learning
codes.reason: Art technique serves Develop and Refine Creative Work and Communicate Visually; the Portrait has no skill for art-form technique itself.

codes.name: Critical Thinking, Inquiry & Media Literacy
codes.reason: Evaluating sources, inquiry and media literacy are the Think Critically skills; one 3.3.0 code spreads across five of them.

codes.name: Early Learning & School Readiness
codes.reason: Covers children below kindergarten age; the Portrait stages start at kindergarten.

codes.name: Academic Engagement Behaviors
codes.reason: Coming prepared and finishing homework touch Plan and Manage My Time; class participation touches Engage in Discussion. Much of the code is participation itself.

codes.name: Academic Perseverance
codes.reason: Sticking with hard schoolwork is Navigate Challenges and Adapt Through Change.

codes.name: Learning Strategies & Study Skills
codes.reason: Study methods and planners are Plan and Manage My Time and Monitor My Progress; test preparation is Strengthen Academic Skills and Prepare for Assessments.

codes.name: Academic Mindsets & Self-Efficacy
codes.reason: A growth mindset touches seeing setbacks as chances to learn; academic self-belief has no Portrait skill.

codes.name: Attendance & School Stability
codes.reason: A status result; the Portrait describes skills.

codes.name: Exclusionary Discipline
codes.reason: A status result; the Portrait describes skills.

codes.name: Grades, Credits & On-Track Status
codes.reason: A status result. The nearest skill is Strengthen Academic Skills and Prepare for Assessments but that is the skill not the grade.

codes.name: Advanced Coursework & Dual Credit
codes.reason: Taking coursework and concurrent enrollment as steps of a plan fits Plan and Take Steps Toward My Future; enrollment alone is a status.

codes.name: High School Completion & Re-engagement
codes.reason: A status result; the Portrait describes the graduate's skills not graduation itself.

codes.name: Postsecondary Enrollment, Persistence & Completion
codes.reason: A status after high school; the Portrait describes skills.

codes.name: Engagement, Interest & Creative Expression
codes.reason: Too broad to place; most of the domain is enjoyment and interest.

codes.name: Enjoyment & Joy
codes.reason: A feeling about the program; the Portrait describes skills.

codes.name: Curiosity & Triggered Interest
codes.reason: Asking questions out of curiosity is the early stages of Ask Questions; curiosity as a feeling has no skill.

codes.name: Sustained & Individual Interest
codes.reason: Pursuing a topic and naming what to learn next touch Connect What I'm Learning to What Matters to Me.

codes.name: Relevance & Utility Value
codes.reason: Seeing learning as useful for one's goals is Connect What I'm Learning to What Matters to Me.

codes.name: Creative Expression & Performance
codes.reason: Making and presenting creative work touches Develop and Refine Creative Work, Communicate Visually and Craft Stories; the code is the experience not a stated skill.

codes.name: Participation in Enriching Activities
codes.reason: Joining clubs or teams to meet new people is a stage of Build and Draw on My Network; returning to a program is participation.

codes.name: Belonging & Relationships
codes.reason: Too broad to place; most of the domain is relationships a young person has.

codes.name: Belonging & Mattering
codes.reason: Feeling one belongs. Foster Belonging is making others feel they belong; they are different results.

codes.name: Supportive Adult Relationships
codes.reason: Fits Build and Draw on My Network only when the young person seeks out and uses a mentor; having a caring adult is a relationship received.

codes.name: Peer Relationships & Friendship
codes.reason: The 11.2 version has no friendship or relationship skill.

codes.name: Family Relationships
codes.reason: The Portrait has no family relationship skill.

codes.name: Social Capital & Networks
codes.reason: Using a wider network for opportunities is Build and Draw on My Network.

codes.name: Social & Emotional Skills (CASEL)
codes.reason: Social and emotional skills with none named sit across Persist and Adapt, Dialogue and Advocacy and Collaborate at the competency level.

codes.name: Emotion Awareness
codes.reason: Naming one's emotions is the first part of Manage My Emotions, Stress and Impulses.

codes.name: Emotion Regulation & Coping
codes.reason: Managing emotions and coping with stress is Manage My Emotions, Stress and Impulses.

codes.name: Goal-Setting, Organization & Self-Discipline
codes.reason: Organization and follow-through are Plan and Manage My Time; goals and adjusting are Monitor My Progress; persistence is Navigate Challenges.

codes.name: Empathy, Perspective-Taking & Social Awareness
codes.reason: Understanding others' perspectives is Engage in Discussion; responding to others' feelings with care is Foster Belonging.

codes.name: Respect for Diversity & Cultural Competence
codes.reason: Including people of other backgrounds touches Foster Belonging and listening across differences; bias awareness has no single skill.

codes.name: Communication & Public Speaking
codes.reason: Public speaking is Present to an Audience and Choose and Introduce My Message; active listening is Engage in Discussion.

codes.name: Teamwork, Collaboration & Group Leadership
codes.reason: Teamwork and leading within a team are the Collaborate skills; one 3.3.0 code spreads across all four.

codes.name: Relationship-Building & Conflict Resolution
codes.reason: Resolving conflict and repairing relationships is Navigate Difficult Conversations and Navigate Conflicts on a team.

codes.name: Help-Seeking & Offering Support
codes.reason: Asking for help touches Advocate for Myself, knowing who to ask touches Build and Draw on My Network, and seeking support for mental health touches Care for My Well-Being.

codes.name: Decision-Making & Problem-Solving
codes.reason: Working a problem through from naming it to acting is the Solve Problems skills; weighing consequences also touches Ethical Choices.

codes.name: Ethical & Prosocial Choices
codes.reason: An ethical choice in the moment is Act with Integrity; standing up for a classmate is Advocate for Others.

codes.name: Risk Avoidance & Refusal Skills
codes.reason: Resisting pressure touches managing impulses; avoiding unsafe situations has no Portrait skill.

codes.name: Identity, Confidence & Agency
codes.reason: Too broad to place; most of the domain is identity and confidence.

codes.name: Self-Understanding & Identity Exploration
codes.reason: Articulating one's values fits Know My Values and Aspirations; identity exploration has no skill in the 11.2 version.

codes.name: Cultural & Social Identity
codes.reason: The 11.2 version dropped the identity and heritage skill that the Beacon version has.

codes.name: Domain Identity
codes.reason: Seeing oneself as a kind of person in a field has no Portrait skill.

codes.name: Confidence, Self-Efficacy & Self-Worth
codes.reason: A belief about oneself. The nearest skill is taking healthy risks under Navigate Challenges but confidence is not a skill in the Portrait.

codes.name: Purpose & Future Orientation
codes.reason: Aspirations and a sense of purpose are Know My Values and Aspirations.

codes.name: Agency, Self-Determination & Self-Advocacy
codes.reason: Advocating for one's own needs and directing one's supports is Advocate for Myself.

codes.name: Character, Values & Civic Life
codes.reason: Civic or character results with none named sit under Global Citizen and Ethical Choices at the competency level.

codes.name: Positive Values & Character
codes.reason: Living out values touches Act with Integrity and Know My Values; character traits as such are not skills.

codes.name: Civic Knowledge
codes.reason: Knowing how government and elections work is Participate in Civic and Democratic Life.

codes.name: Critical Consciousness & Social Justice
codes.reason: Recognizing and challenging patterns of injustice is the upper stages of Advocate for Others; analyzing issues across perspectives is Examine Global Issues.

codes.name: Civic Voice, Leadership & Participation
codes.reason: Influencing collective decisions is Participate in Civic and Democratic Life; advocacy for change is Advocate for Others.

codes.name: Community Service & Action
codes.reason: Identifying a community issue and acting on it is Take Action to Improve My Community.

codes.name: Environmental Stewardship
codes.reason: Weighing one's impact on the environment touches Weigh the Impact of My Choices; connection to nature has no skill.

codes.name: Digital Citizenship & Online Safety
codes.reason: Online safety and respectful conduct are Healthy Online Communities and Use Technology and AI Ethically.

codes.name: Career & Economic Readiness
codes.reason: Career readiness with none named sits under Plan and Navigate My Postsecondary Future at the competency level.

codes.name: Career Awareness & Exploration
codes.reason: Exploring careers and interests is Explore My Interests and Investigate Postsecondary and Career Pathways.

codes.name: College & Career Transition Knowledge
codes.reason: Applications and financial aid are Plan and Take Steps; resumes and interviews are Craft My Application Materials and Interview with Confidence. The few application portfolio statements would fit Curate My Portfolio, a second-pass question.

codes.name: Employability & Workplace Skills
codes.reason: Workplace communication is Communicate Across Workplace Settings; professional conduct is Navigate New Settings.

codes.name: Technical Skills, Credentials & Work-Based Learning
codes.reason: Credentials and internships as steps of a plan fit Plan and Take Steps; trade skills themselves have no Portrait skill.

codes.name: Employment & Earnings
codes.reason: A status result; the Portrait describes skills.

codes.name: Financial Capability
codes.reason: Budgeting saving and credit are Manage My Money.

codes.name: Independent Living Skills
codes.reason: Cooking transport and documents have no Portrait skill; money skills alone go to Financial Capability.

codes.name: Health, Safety & Well-Being
codes.reason: Too broad to place; most of the domain is health conditions and services.

codes.name: Healthy Daily Habits
codes.reason: Activity nutrition sleep and screen time habits are Care for My Well-Being.

codes.name: Motor & Sport Skills
codes.reason: The Portrait has no physical skill.

codes.name: Health Knowledge & Safety Skills
codes.reason: Health knowledge touches Care for My Well-Being and finding reliable health information touches Find and Evaluate Information; first aid has no skill.

codes.name: Sexual & Reproductive Health
codes.reason: Health behavior touches Care for My Well-Being; the Portrait does not name sexual health.

codes.name: Health Care Access & Condition Management
codes.reason: Receiving care is a service result not a skill.

codes.name: Mental Health Symptoms & Distress
codes.reason: A symptom level not a skill; coping skills go to Emotion Regulation.

codes.name: Flourishing & Life Satisfaction
codes.reason: A state of well-being not a skill; the habits that support it go to Healthy Daily Habits.

codes.name: Healing & Trauma Recovery
codes.reason: A recovery result not a skill.

codes.name: Mental Health Service Access & Use
codes.reason: Using services is a service result not a skill.

codes.name: Felt Safety
codes.reason: A feeling not a skill.

codes.name: Substance Use
codes.reason: A behavior result the Portrait does not name.

codes.name: Violence, Bullying & Victimization
codes.reason: An incidence result the Portrait does not name.

codes.name: Justice Involvement, Diversion & Reentry
codes.reason: A status result the Portrait does not name.
